newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain, China fail to break deadlock on HK troops.
newsitem.headline: Britain, China fail to break deadlock on HK troops.

text.p: British and Chinese negotiators failed on Tuesday to break a deadlock over China's demand to send an advance party of troops to Hong Kong before Beijing formally takes over the territory on July 1.
After two days of talks on the sticky issue, the two sides failed to reach an agreement, diplomats said.

The haggling over troops at the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) diplomatic talks on handover arrangements was the latest of many disputes in the run-up to the change of sovereignty at midnight on June 30, the end of more than 150 years of British rule.
British negotiator Alan Paul told reporters he would not want to put a deadline on resolving the issue, but made clear little progress had been made.

"We hope to resolve the issue as soon as possible but I wouldn't want to put a deadline on it at the moment," Paul said. "I think through patient discussion and friendly consultations we should be able to find out the difficulties."

Britain has called on China to slash the number and delay the arrival date of the advance military party. Neither side has revealed the size of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) contingent China wants to send in before the actual handover.
China has said its garrison might be as large as Britain's was at its peak a decade ago at around 10,000 personnel.
The elite PLA unit has been deployed over the border in the Chinese zone of Shenzhen in recent months, undergoing rigorous military and educational training for its mission.
